cp02_reconciliation.contradiction: D4C said CP-A3/radio_hw is BEFORE D2/D3, but also said CP-O2 has PSM running and DMA initialized (D3A0). These cannot both hold for the same vendor-time state.
cp02_reconciliation.resolution: wlc_bmac_radio_hw is an RPC-dispatched function (WLRPC_WLC_BMAC_RADIO_HW_ID) with no in-corpus caller. It is NOT executed during the vendor Linux attach/init; therefore there is no vendor-time CP-O2 to order. The D4C 'CP-O2' state was an unjustified inference.

cp02_reconciliation.C_proposed_openbrcm_after_D3: PSM running (D2A), DMA engines initialized (D3A0), MAC per initvals, then radio ON
cp02_reconciliation.D_note: C is HYPOTHETICAL: the vendor does not invoke wlc_bmac_radio_hw in this corpus.

external_caller.layer: offload / RPC layer (bcm_ol); RPC ID WLRPC_WLC_BMAC_RADIO_HW_ID
external_caller.conclusion: wlc_bmac_radio_hw is an RPC-dispatch target, not a C-called attach/init function. Its caller is the RPC/offload layer (or the peer firmware), not present in the available corpora.
